clue.text: Male animal a thousand and eight, perhaps, or roundabout

indicators.note: roundabout means going round the other way, so the cube and the word or are read backwards together

parts.note: eight is two cubed, so it is an example of a cube
taken as written
K is the usual abbreviation for a thousand

explanation.surface: A riddle about counting some male creature, a thousand and eight or thereabouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' looks like 'approximately' but turns CUBE and OR backwards to give ROEBUC; 'eight, perhaps' is a cube because 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is the male of the roe deer, so it is a male animal.

clue.text: Deodorant that's sweet covering bottom of genital region, finally

indicators.note: covering means the sweet wraps around the next letter

parts.note: Rolo is a British brand of chocolate-covered toffee sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter
finally asks for the closing letter of the word region

explanation.surface: A deodorant that's pleasant applied to the lower body.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolos are small chocolate caramels sold in the UK; the L of genital goes inside, then the N of region.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll-on is a deodorant applied with a rolling ball.

clue.text: Artist into 18 16

indicators.note: into says the artist's name lies inside the answers to entries 18 and 16 run together

explanation.surface: An artist who is keen on parties and angels.
explanation.walkthrough: Write the answers to 18 across and 16 down side by side and the artist's name straddles the join.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist known for impossible buildings.

clue.text: Nude stupid to wobble about, it's beyond question

indicators.note: to wobble about suggests the letters of nude stupid shake into a new order

explanation.surface: A naked fool wobbling around is a certainty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undisputed is not argued over, so it is certain and accepted.

clue.text: Artist — something cocked up?

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: one cocks a snook, a rude gesture of thumb to nose

explanation.surface: An artist's work is something botched?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cocked up' looks like British slang for botched; read 'something cocked' as SNOOK and 'up' as the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeff Koons is an American artist famous for balloon-animal sculptures.

clue.text: At first, stink smelt — when one did so?

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word stink

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell, so one who niffed gave off a pong

explanation.surface: A stink was noticed at once, and we wonder who was sniffing at the time.
explanation.walkthrough: NIFF is British slang for a bad smell; the riddle half asks what someone did when there was a smell about.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell something is to sniff it, so smelt can stand for sniffed in the sense of detecting an odour.

clue.text: As net unravelling about artist, it decreases

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the artist's name
unravelling says the letters of as net come apart and are rewoven

parts.note: Joan Miro was a Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A net unravels around an artist as it shrinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unravelling' turns AS NET into STEAN, with MIRO inside before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The appliance removes creases from clothes, so it de-creases them: a pun on reducing.

clue.text: Very short distance by which winger misses header

indicators.note: in a down clue the header is the top letter, which is missed off

parts.note: a winger is something with wings, here a finch

explanation.surface: A winger misses a header by a tiny margin.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface misleads: a winger is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a small unit of length, a very short distance.

clue.text: Artist's taken in hand by a supporter?

indicators.note: taken in means the artist is held inside the word for hand

parts.note: a closed hand is a fist
Tracey Emin is a British artist

explanation.surface: An artist is held by the hand of a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Tracey Emin is a British artist known for My Bed; she goes inside FIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who advocates women's rights is a supporter of that cause.

clue.text: Identification not written down, Ottoman governor in call for help proves defiant

indicators.note: in a down clue not written down means written upwards, reversed
in means the governor sits inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the distress call
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: Lacking written identification, an Ottoman governor shouting for help shows defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not written down' sounds like undocumented, but in a down clue it reverses ID to DI.
explanation.definitionFit: To disobey is to refuse orders, so disobeys means acts defiantly.

clue.text: Clear water, say, lid removed to keep cold

indicators.note: to keep means the shortened liquid holds the next letter inside it
in an across clue the lid is the first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: water is an example of a fluid
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Clear water once the lid is off, kept chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lid removed' drops the F from FLUID to leave LUID, and 'to keep' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucid means clear, as in a lucid explanation that is easy to understand.

clue.text: Finished, leader in charge having some appalling defeats

parts.note: something finished is over

indicators.note: leader in asks for the opening letter of the word charge
appalling suggests the word some is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: With the job done, the person in charge has had some appalling defeats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges SOME into OMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to beat them, so overcomes is a synonym of defeats.

clue.text: Poem seen as nonsensical magic words

indicators.note: nonsensical says the letters of poem seen as make no sense until rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem regarded as nonsense is called a magic incantation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Ali Baba that opens the robbers' cave is the classic set of magic words.

clue.text: Someone pretentious reviewing Japanese art, less than perfect

indicators.note: reviewing is read as re-viewing, looking back, so the trimmed word is turned round
AI (A1) means first-rate or perfect, so less than perfect asks for those letters to be taken away

parts.note: bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees

explanation.surface: A pretentious person reviews Japanese art and finds it short of perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands for A1, first-class; 'less than perfect' takes it from BONSAI to leave BONS, and 'reviewing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A snob is a person who looks down on others and affects superior taste, so is pretentious.

clue.text: Supporter has complaint about new player

indicators.note: about means the complaint wraps round the letter for new

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
an actor plays parts

explanation.surface: A backer complains about a new actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor gives money or help, so is a supporter or patron.

clue.text: How one's eyes could implode in a serious way?

definitions.meaning: the eye is filled with vitreous and aqueous humour, so without that fluid it would collapse
acting with no sense of fun, gravely and solemnly

explanation.walkthrough: Humour here is the old word for a body fluid; the eyeball holds its shape because of the humours inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without any sense of fun is doing it soberly, a serious manner.

clue.text: She's enslaved artist in temple, topless

indicators.note: in means the artist is placed inside the trimmed building
in a down clue topless means losing the top letter

parts.note: a mosque is a Muslim place of worship, a temple
Salvador Dali was a Spanish surrealist painter

explanation.surface: A slave girl and an artist in a temple, without her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the top letter of the temple word, leaving OSQUE, and 'in' puts the surrealist inside; the surface's 'topless' suggests undress, not a missing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An odalisque was a female slave or concubine in a harem.

clue.text: More than one angel fish swallowing ruler, 100 cm

indicators.note: swallowing means the fish takes the ruler inside it

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a ruler
100 centimetres is one metre, written as I (one) and M (metre)

explanation.surface: A fish eats a ruler a metre long.
explanation.walkthrough: '100 cm' is one metre: I for one and M for metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubim is the plural of cherub, a kind of angel.

clue.text: Soldier given list of duties, short of a bunk

parts.note: Tommy is a nickname for a British soldier

indicators.note: short of means the list lacks the letter that follows

parts.note: a rota lists who does which duty when

explanation.surface: A soldier given his duty roster lacks a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk' looks like a bed but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot and bunk are both slang for nonsense.

clue.text: Tip taken from beak joining nurses for parties

indicators.note: the tip is the end letter, which is cut off the word for a nose

parts.note: beak and hooter are both slang for the nose
nannies are children's nurses

explanation.surface: A tip is taken off a bird's beak and given to nurses who are partying.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOTER loses its last letter R to give HOOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hootenanny is an informal party or gathering, often with folk music.

clue.text: Another story that's translated through incomplete personality

indicators.note: through means the French word runs through the shortened self
incomplete means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: one's self is one's personality
que is the French for that

explanation.surface: A further tale is translated by a personality lacking something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' leaves SEL, and 'through' threads the French word for 'that' inside it; 'translated' signals the French, not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is a follow-on book or film, another story continuing the first.

clue.text: Relies on mystery, ultimately, this artist?

parts.note: one who relies on something banks on it

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the word mystery

explanation.surface: This artist depends on staying mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is the anonymous British street artist, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksy is a pseudonymous street artist whose identity remains unknown.

clue.text: More difficult, far more than a day's work

definitions.text: far more than a day's work

indicators.note: difficult hints at the word more being troublesome, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Something harder, much more than one day's labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges MORE. The definition alludes to the saying that Rome was not built in a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Building the Italian capital proverbially took longer than one day, so it was far more than a day's work.

clue.text: Old shooter is caught doubled up in embrace of US girl, artist

indicators.note: in embrace of means the following letters are hugged by the girl

parts.note: dame is American slang for a woman
taken as written

indicators.note: doubled up asks for the letter for caught to appear twice

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An old gunman is caught, doubled over in an American girl's arms, along with an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled up' gives two Cs, and 'in embrace of' puts IS and those Cs inside the American slang word after its D. Disc cameras were a 1980s Kodak format.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc camera was a 1980s Kodak format, an outmoded device for taking shots.

clue.text: Good to support Conservative member — it's his policy

definitions.text: Good to support Conservative member — it's his policy

indicators.note: in a down clue to support means the letter sits below the others

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member

explanation.surface: A politician whose policy is backing a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats into coalition with the Conservatives in 2010, propping up their government.
explanation.definitionFit: As coalition deputy prime minister, the Lib Dem leader made backing the Tory government his policy.

clue.text: County wards have them

definitions.meaning: The standard short form of Bedfordshire, an English county
hospital wards are lined with places for patients to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Bedfordshire is shortened in addresses, and hospital wards contain rows of sleeping furniture.

clue.text: Back massage to accompany promiscuous 19 as acts of titillation

indicators.note: back says the word for a massage is reversed

parts.note: to massage is to rub

indicators.note: promiscuous means mixed indiscriminately, so the letters of entry 19 are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 19 down, another story that follows on

explanation.surface: A back rub goes with a racy follow-up in scenes of titillation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' turns RUB to BUR; 'promiscuous' rearranges SEQUEL to LESQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlesque is a variety show with striptease and comic sexual innuendo, so a set of titillating acts.

clue.text: The case of the gigantic beast?

definitions.text: The case of the gigantic beast?

parts.words: The case of the gigantic beast?
parts.note: a case is a large travelling box, and an elephant's long nose shares that name

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a detective case; the reading wanted is a travelling chest that is also an elephant's nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk is a big luggage case, and also the long nose of an elephant, a huge animal.

clue.text: Artist taking single vessel into China

indicators.note: into means the next letters are placed inside the word for friend

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), a friend
I is the Roman numeral one, a single
SS is steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: An artist takes a single ship to China.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri Matisse was a French painter; China, capitalised to look like the country, is rhyming slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Matisse was a French painter and leader of Fauvism, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Artist's bloody outstanding rotating tree

indicators.note: outstanding is read as standing outside, so the word for bloody goes round the rest

parts.note: something bloody is gory

indicators.note: rotating says the tree name is turned round

parts.note: the elm is a tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' turns ELM to MLE. Antony Gormley is the British sculptor of the Angel of the North.
